# Chrome DevTools CLI for agents: drive the browser from the terminal

Curated by Skill Harbor — @chromedevtools's skill for the chrome-devtools-mcp CLI: write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate Chrome from your terminal. The AI workflow is Execute → Inspect → Act: list and select pages, take accessibility-tree snapshots to get element UIDs, then click, fill, type, press keys, drag, hover, handle dialogs and upload files; navigate pages, create tabs, reload, emulate network conditions, CPU throttling, geolocation, color scheme, viewport and user agent; record performance traces with insights, capture and compare heap snapshots (memory-debugging flag), list and fetch network requests and console messages, evaluate JavaScript, run Lighthouse audits, take screenshots (viewport, full-page or element), manage extensions, and install/launch PWAs. Output is Markdown-like text by default (JSON with a flag). Honest caveats: the one-time installation is a prerequisite, covered in the repo's references/installation.md — not part of the AI workflow; note the CLI defaults to full filesystem access (--allowUnrestrictedPaths=true) — pass false deliberately to sandbox it to the OS temp directory. Apache-2.0 licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
